header:
Reset your money
in one weekend

lines.text: People guessed $86 for subscriptions. It was $219.
lines.say: People guessed eighty-six dollars for subscriptions. It was two-nineteen.

lines.text: That's a 2022 survey of 1,000 people. Itemized, subscriptions ran $133 a month more than they guessed.
lines.say: That's a twenty twenty-two survey of a thousand people. Itemized, subscriptions ran a hundred thirty-three dollars a month more than they guessed.

lines.text: Same survey: 42% had forgotten they were still paying for something they no longer used.
lines.say: Same survey: forty-two percent had forgotten they were still paying for something they no longer used.

lines.text: That's the thing about money. Most leaks aren't dramatic. They're quiet, and they're on autopay.
lines.say: That's the thing about money. Most leaks aren't dramatic. They're quiet, and they're on autopay.

lines.text: So here's the plan: one weekend, eight steps, and your money goes from foggy to clear.
lines.say: So here's the plan: one weekend, eight steps, and your money goes from foggy to clear.

lines.text: Saturday is about seeing. Sunday is about setting things up so they run without you.
lines.say: Saturday is about seeing. Sunday is about setting things up so they run without you.

lines.text: You don't need a finance degree. You need your logins, a notebook, and maybe coffee.
lines.say: You don't need a finance degree. You need your logins, a notebook, and maybe coffee.

lines.text: Quick note: this is education, not advice. Every number here comes with its date.
lines.say: Quick note: this is education, not advice. Every number here comes with its date.

lines.text: Saturday morning: the snapshot.
lines.say: Saturday morning: the snapshot.

lines.text: Step one is a list. Every account you have, and what's in it or what you owe on it.
lines.say: Step one is a list. Every account you have, and what's in it or what you owe on it.

lines.text: Checking and savings first. Those are easy.
lines.say: Checking and savings first. Those are easy.

lines.text: Then retirement accounts, including that old 401(k) from a job you left years ago.
lines.say: Then retirement accounts, including that old four oh one k from a job you left years ago.

lines.text: Then every debt: cards, car loan, student loans, the store card you opened for 15% off a couch.
lines.say: Then every debt: cards, car loan, student loans, the store card you opened for fifteen percent off a couch.

lines.text: Now one subtraction. Everything you own, minus everything you owe. That's your net worth.
lines.say: Now one subtraction. Everything you own, minus everything you owe. That's your net worth.

lines.text: Let's do an example. Checking $1,800, savings $2,400, and a 401(k) with $9,300. That's $13,500.
lines.say: Let's do an example. Checking eighteen hundred dollars, savings twenty-four hundred, and a four oh one k with ninety-three hundred. That's thirteen thousand five hundred.

lines.text: On the other side: a $6,000 card, a $1,000 store card, and a $9,000 car loan. That's $16,000.
lines.say: On the other side: a six thousand dollar card, a one thousand dollar store card, and a nine thousand dollar car loan. That's sixteen thousand.

lines.text: $13,500 minus $16,000 is negative $2,500.
lines.say: Thirteen thousand five hundred minus sixteen thousand is negative twenty-five hundred dollars.

lines.text: And that's fine. Plenty of people start below zero, especially with a car loan or student debt.
lines.say: And that's fine. Plenty of people start below zero, especially with a car loan or student debt.

lines.text: It's not a grade. Write it down with the date, so next January you can compare.
lines.say: It's not a grade. Write it down with the date, so next January you can compare.

lines.text: Bonus: making the list is how people find forgotten accounts, like that old 401(k) still sitting with a former employer.
lines.say: Bonus: making the list is how people find forgotten accounts, like that old four oh one k still sitting with a former employer.

lines.text: Saturday afternoon: follow the money.
lines.say: Saturday afternoon: follow the money.

lines.text: Step two: pull up last month's bank and card statements. Not a budget app. The actual statements.
lines.say: Step two: pull up last month's bank and card statements. Not a budget app. The actual statements.

lines.text: Go line by line and sort every charge into three piles.
lines.say: Go line by line and sort every charge into three piles.

lines.text: Must pay: rent, utilities, insurance, minimum payments.
lines.say: Must pay: rent, utilities, insurance, minimum payments.

lines.text: Want: takeout, streaming, the gym you actually go to.
lines.say: Want: takeout, streaming, the gym you actually go to.

lines.text: And wait, what? That's the charge you don't recognize, or forgot you signed up for.
lines.say: And wait, what? That's the charge you don't recognize, or forgot you signed up for.

lines.text: Remember the survey: people guessed $86 a month, but itemized, it was $219.
lines.say: Remember the survey: people guessed eighty-six dollars a month, but itemized, it was two hundred nineteen.

lines.text: That $133 gap, times 12 months, is $1,596 a year. That's our math on the survey average.
lines.say: That hundred thirty-three dollar gap, times twelve months, is fifteen hundred ninety-six dollars a year. That's our math on the survey average.

lines.text: Why does it happen? In that survey, 86% had some or all of their subscriptions on autopay. Out of sight, out of mind.
lines.say: Why does it happen? In that survey, eighty-six percent had some or all of their subscriptions on autopay. Out of sight, out of mind.

lines.text: So for each one in the want and wait-what piles, ask one question: did I use this last month?
lines.say: So for each one in the want and wait-what piles, ask one question: did I use this last month?

lines.text: If the answer is no, that's a candidate to cancel. If it's yes, keep it guilt-free. This isn't about joy cuts.
lines.say: If the answer is no, that's a candidate to cancel. If it's yes, keep it guilt-free. This isn't about joy cuts.

lines.text: One more thing to look for: fees. Overdraft fees, late fees, ATM fees. Those are leaks too.
lines.say: One more thing to look for: fees. Overdraft fees, late fees, ATM fees. Those are leaks too.

lines.text: Total up what you cut. That number has a job in step four.
lines.say: Total up what you cut. That number has a job in step four.

lines.text: Saturday night: the debt list.
lines.say: Saturday night: the debt list.

lines.text: Step three: take every debt from your snapshot and add two things: the interest rate, and the minimum payment.
lines.say: Step three: take every debt from your snapshot and add two things: the interest rate, and the minimum payment.

lines.text: The rate is called the APR, and it's on your statement. This number matters more than the balance.
lines.say: The rate is called the A P R, and it's on your statement. This number matters more than the balance.

lines.text: Here's why. The Fed tracks the average rate on credit cards that actually charged interest.
lines.say: Here's why. The Fed tracks the average rate on credit cards that actually charged interest.

lines.text: In August 2022 it was 18.43%. By August 2024 it hit 23.37%, the highest in data going back to 1994.
lines.say: In August twenty twenty-two it was eighteen point four three percent. By August twenty twenty-four it hit twenty-three point three seven, the highest in data going back to nineteen ninety-four.

lines.text: In August 2026, it was still 22.36%.
lines.say: In August twenty twenty-six, it was still twenty-two point three six percent.

lines.text: Some cards charge even more. Take a $6,000 balance at 28%.
lines.say: Some cards charge even more. Take a six thousand dollar balance at twenty-eight percent.

lines.text: $6,000 times 28%, divided by 12, is $140 of interest in a single month.
lines.say: Six thousand times twenty-eight percent, divided by twelve, is a hundred forty dollars of interest in a single month.

lines.text: Now the question everyone asks: which debt do I pay extra on first? There are two classic methods.
lines.say: Now the question everyone asks: which debt do I pay extra on first? There are two classic methods.

lines.text: Avalanche: pay minimums on everything, then every extra dollar goes to the highest rate.
lines.say: Avalanche: pay minimums on everything, then every extra dollar goes to the highest rate.

lines.text: Snowball: minimums on everything, then extra goes to the smallest balance, for a quick win.
lines.say: Snowball: minimums on everything, then extra goes to the smallest balance, for a quick win.

lines.text: Let's run real numbers. Card A: $1,000 at 15%, minimum $40. Card B: $6,000 at 28%, minimum $120.
lines.say: Let's run real numbers. Card A: one thousand dollars at fifteen percent, minimum forty. Card B: six thousand at twenty-eight percent, minimum a hundred twenty.

lines.text: You put $400 a month toward both. That's the minimums, plus $240 extra.
lines.say: You put four hundred dollars a month toward both. That's the minimums, plus two hundred forty extra.

lines.text: With the avalanche, the extra goes to Card B. Total interest: $1,877. Debt-free in 23 months.
lines.say: With the avalanche, the extra goes to Card B. Total interest: eighteen hundred seventy-seven dollars. Debt-free in twenty-three months.

lines.text: With the snowball, Card A is gone by month 4, but total interest is $2,060. Same 23 months.
lines.say: With the snowball, Card A is gone by month four, but total interest is two thousand sixty. Same twenty-three months.

lines.text: The difference is $183 in our math. The avalanche saves money. The snowball buys an early win.
lines.say: The difference is a hundred eighty-three dollars in our math. The avalanche saves money. The snowball buys an early win.

lines.text: Which is better? The one you'll actually stick with. Pick one tonight and write the order down.
lines.say: Which is better? The one you'll actually stick with. Pick one tonight and write the order down.

lines.text: Sunday morning: put it on autopilot.
lines.say: Sunday morning: put it on autopilot.

lines.text: Sunday is about systems. Willpower runs out. Automatic transfers don't.
lines.say: Sunday is about systems. Willpower runs out. Automatic transfers don't.

lines.text: Step four is savings. Set an automatic transfer from checking to savings on payday, even a small one.
lines.say: Step four is savings. Set an automatic transfer from checking to savings on payday, even a small one.

lines.text: That's where the money you cut in step two can go. Cancel a $15 subscription, move $15.
lines.say: That's where the money you cut in step two can go. Cancel a fifteen dollar subscription, move fifteen dollars.

lines.text: Why bother? In the Fed's 2025 household survey, 63% of adults said they'd cover a $400 surprise with cash or its equivalent.
lines.say: Why bother? In the Fed's twenty twenty-five household survey, sixty-three percent of adults said they'd cover a four hundred dollar surprise with cash or its equivalent.

lines.text: For adults 18 to 29, it was just 45%.
lines.say: For adults eighteen to twenty-nine, it was just forty-five percent.

lines.text: Emergency funds are a separate topic, so here's the short version: a cushion keeps a surprise off your credit card.
lines.say: Emergency funds are a separate topic, so here's the short version: a cushion keeps a surprise off your credit card.

lines.text: Step five is retirement. If your job offers a 401(k) match, check what percent you contribute today.
lines.say: Step five is retirement. If your job offers a four oh one k match, check what percent you contribute today.

lines.text: In Vanguard's 2026 report, the average promised match was 4.7% of pay in 2025.
lines.say: In Vanguard's twenty twenty-six report, the average promised match was four point seven percent of pay in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Here's an example plan: it matches 100% of what you put in, up to 4% of pay, and you earn $50,000.
lines.say: Here's an example plan: it matches a hundred percent of what you put in, up to four percent of pay, and you earn fifty thousand dollars.

lines.text: Put in 4%, or $2,000 a year, and the employer adds $2,000.
lines.say: Put in four percent, or two thousand dollars a year, and the employer adds two thousand.

lines.text: Put in only 2%, and the match is $1,000. That's $1,000 a year left on the table.
lines.say: Put in only two percent, and the match is one thousand. That's a thousand dollars a year left on the table.

lines.text: Your plan's formula may be different, so look it up in your benefits portal. It takes five minutes.
lines.say: Your plan's formula may be different, so look it up in your benefits portal. It takes five minutes.

lines.text: Now the limits. For 2026, the most you could put into a 401(k) yourself was $24,500.
lines.say: Now the limits. For twenty twenty-six, the most you could put into a four oh one k yourself was twenty-four thousand five hundred dollars.

lines.text: And for 2026, the IRA limit was $7,500.
lines.say: And for twenty twenty-six, the I R A limit was seven thousand five hundred.

lines.text: The IRS usually raises these for the new year, so check its 2027 numbers before you change anything.
lines.say: The I R S usually raises these for the new year, so check its twenty twenty-seven numbers before you change anything.

lines.text: Most people never get near those limits. The point is just that your percent doesn't raise itself.
lines.say: Most people never get near those limits. The point is just that your percent doesn't raise itself.

lines.text: Some plans have an auto-increase option that bumps you up 1% a year. Worth a look while you're logged in.
lines.say: Some plans have an auto-increase option that bumps you up one percent a year. Worth a look while you're logged in.

lines.text: Last autopilot move: set every bill to at least the minimum payment on autopay, so a late fee never happens.
lines.say: Last autopilot move: set every bill to at least the minimum payment on autopay, so a late fee never happens.

lines.text: Sunday afternoon: lock it down.
lines.say: Sunday afternoon: lock it down.

lines.text: Step six is protection, starting with your credit reports.
lines.say: Step six is protection, starting with your credit reports.

lines.text: You can get your reports from all three bureaus free, every week, at AnnualCreditReport.com. That's been permanent since October 2023.
lines.say: You can get your reports from all three bureaus free, every week, at Annual Credit Report dot com. That's been permanent since October twenty twenty-three.

lines.text: That's the only site authorized for those free reports, per the FTC. Lookalike sites may charge.
lines.say: That's the only site authorized for those free reports, per the FTC. Lookalike sites may charge.

lines.text: Scan for accounts you don't recognize, wrong addresses, or late payments that aren't yours.
lines.say: Scan for accounts you don't recognize, wrong addresses, or late payments that aren't yours.

lines.text: Reading a report in depth is a separate topic. Today's step is just: pull it and look.
lines.say: Reading a report in depth is a separate topic. Today's step is just: pull it and look.

lines.text: Next, consider a credit freeze. It stops new lenders from pulling your report, which makes it much harder to open credit in your name.
lines.say: Next, consider a credit freeze. It stops new lenders from pulling your report, which makes it much harder to open credit in your name.

lines.text: Since September 21, 2018, freezing and unfreezing is free by federal law.
lines.say: Since September twenty-first, twenty eighteen, freezing and unfreezing is free by federal law.

lines.text: You do it at each of the three bureaus: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion.
lines.say: You do it at each of the three bureaus: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion.

lines.text: A freeze doesn't hurt your score. And when you apply for a loan, you lift it for free first.
lines.say: A freeze doesn't hurt your score. And when you apply for a loan, you lift it for free first.

lines.text: Watch out: bureaus also sell lock products. The FTC notes locks can carry fees. The free one is the freeze.
lines.say: Watch out: bureaus also sell lock products. The FTC notes locks can carry fees. The free one is the freeze.

lines.text: Step seven is insurance. Open your renters or homeowners, auto, and health policies, and check two things.
lines.say: Step seven is insurance. Open your renters or homeowners, auto, and health policies, and check two things.

lines.text: Does the coverage still fit your life, and when does each policy renew? Put those dates in your notebook.
lines.say: Does the coverage still fit your life, and when does each policy renew? Put those dates in your notebook.

lines.text: Last, beneficiaries. On your 401(k), IRA, and life insurance, there's a form naming who gets the money.
lines.say: Last, beneficiaries. On your four oh one k, I R A, and life insurance, there's a form naming who gets the money.

lines.text: Here's the surprise: that form generally beats your will. And it may not update itself after a marriage or a divorce.
lines.say: Here's the surprise: that form generally beats your will. And it may not update itself after a marriage or a divorce.

lines.text: So if your ex is still on there from your first job, this weekend is the time to log in and check.
lines.say: So if your ex is still on there from your first job, this weekend is the time to log in and check.

lines.text: Sunday night: reminders, and the checklist.
lines.say: Sunday night: reminders, and the checklist.

lines.text: Step eight, the final one: open your calendar and set a few reminders, so this weekend isn't a one-time thing.
lines.say: Step eight, the final one: open your calendar and set a few reminders, so this weekend isn't a one-time thing.

lines.text: A 30-minute check every quarter. Net worth, statements, and your debt list.
lines.say: A thirty-minute check every quarter. Net worth, statements, and your debt list.

lines.text: And one hard date: the federal tax deadline for 2026 returns is April 15, 2027.
lines.say: And one hard date: the federal tax deadline for twenty twenty-six returns is April fifteenth, twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: Now the common mistakes. Number one: trying to fix everything in one night. That's why it's a weekend.
lines.say: Now the common mistakes. Number one: trying to fix everything in one night. That's why it's a weekend.

lines.text: Number two: never looking up your match. That five-minute check is the easiest one to skip.
lines.say: Number two: never looking up your match. That five-minute check is the easiest one to skip.

lines.text: Number three: paying for a lock when the freeze is free.
lines.say: Number three: paying for a lock when the freeze is free.

lines.text: And number four: a beneficiary form nobody has looked at since the day you were hired.
lines.say: And number four: a beneficiary form nobody has looked at since the day you were hired.

lines.text: Here's the whole thing on one screen. Saturday: snapshot, statements, debt list.
lines.say: Here's the whole thing on one screen. Saturday: snapshot, statements, debt list.

lines.text: Sunday: autopilot, credit and freeze, insurance and beneficiaries, and reminders.
lines.say: Sunday: autopilot, credit and freeze, insurance and beneficiaries, and reminders.

lines.text: Remember that survey: people underestimated subscriptions by $133 a month. Statements are where you find yours.
lines.say: Remember that survey: people underestimated subscriptions by a hundred thirty-three dollars a month. Statements are where you find yours.

lines.text: And with the average card rate at 22.36%, knowing your APRs is half the battle.
lines.say: And with the average card rate at twenty-two point three six percent, knowing your A P Rs is half the battle.

lines.text: You won't fix your whole financial life in two days. But you'll know exactly where it stands.
lines.say: You won't fix your whole financial life in two days. But you'll know exactly where it stands.

lines.text: And clear beats perfect. Grab a notebook, block out Saturday morning, and start with the list.
lines.say: And clear beats perfect. Grab a notebook, block out Saturday morning, and start with the list.

lines.text: If this helped, subscribe for more step-by-step guides.

post.title: Reset Your Money in One Weekend: An 8-Step Checklist
post.ig: People underestimated their subscriptions by $133 a month (2022 survey). Here's the one-weekend reset that finds yours.
post.tiktok: People underestimated subscriptions by $133 a month in a 2022 survey. The one-weekend money reset, step by step.
post.yt_desc:
In a 2022 survey, people guessed they spent $86 a month on subscriptions; itemized, it averaged $219. This guide walks through a one-weekend money reset: a net worth snapshot with exact math, a statement review, a debt list with a worked avalanche vs snowball example, automatic savings and the 401(k) match, free weekly credit reports and a free credit freeze, insurance and beneficiary checks, and calendar reminders. We chart the Fed's average card rate on accounts charged interest from August 2022 to August 2026, and use 2026 contribution limits (check the IRS for 2027).

CHAPTERS

Sources: C+R Research subscription survey via CNBC (Sept 2022); Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit and FRED (Aug 2022-Aug 2026 readings, Oct 2026 release); Federal Reserve SHED, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025 (May 2026); Vanguard How America Saves 2026; IRS 2026 retirement limits (Nov 2025); FTC on free weekly credit reports (Oct 2023) and free credit freezes (Sept 2018); TaxAct 2027 tax dates.

News and education, not financial advice.
